fields.features_heading: What the Form Settles Before Work Starts
fields.features_subheading: Every answer a client gives once is a call you skip and a document you never have to ask for twice.
fields.feature_1:
Sections that match the services bought

Show payroll questions only to clients who chose payroll, and sales tax questions only to businesses that sell goods. A client buying one personal return sees a short form.
fields.feature_2:
Document requests from the answers

Turn answers into named upload requests. A client who sold shares is asked for a 1099-B, and a partner in a partnership is asked for each Schedule K-1 they received that year.
fields.feature_3:
Quotes priced from the intake

Price each engagement from what the client tells you, with a base fee plus a set amount per K-1 or per added state. A partner can review any quote before the client sees it.
fields.feature_4:
The engagement letter on the last screen

Fill the letter with the quoted fee and the services the client picked, then collect a typed or drawn signature. The signed letter lands in that client's record with a timestamp.
fields.feature_5:
New clients assigned by service

Send each finished intake to whoever owns that work. Payroll setups can reach your payroll lead in Slack, while bookkeeping clients go to the bookkeeper with the fewest accounts.
fields.feature_6:
Code your firm can take with it

Export the full code of the form and its client database to GitHub on paid plans. A developer can later connect it to the client portal or practice software your firm already runs.

fields.usecase_heading: Intake for Four Kinds of Accounting Work
fields.tab_content_1:
Any books six months behind get a catch-up quote

Ledgerline Bookkeeping asks each new client to list every bank and card account with the month it was last reconciled. Harlow Florist lists four. Its business checking was reconciled seven months ago. Any account more than six months behind gets a catch-up quote, and the monthly plan waits until the cleanup is done.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each client's document list comes from their own year

The intake asks individual clients about their year, not about tax forms. Dev Arora ticks a new job and shares sold. The form builds his list of six documents, a 1099-B for the shares among them. Four have arrived. If two are still missing after seven days, he gets a reminder email.
fields.tab_content_3:
The fee is on the engagement letter before work starts

Ostrander CPA prices business returns from the intake. A partnership return starts at $1,200. Each partner's K-1 adds $75, and each added state return adds $150. Brightwater Design has four partners and files in two states, for a quote of $1,650. The managing partner signs the engagement letter with that fee in it.
fields.tab_content_4:
When staff work in two states, the payroll lead steps in

Tidewater Payroll's intake asks a new employer for its pay schedule and the state each employee works in. Fenwick Bakery reports 14 staff: 11 in Ohio and three in Kentucky. A second work state sends the setup to Lena Brooks, the payroll lead, as a Slack message. Single-state employers join the specialist queue.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an Accounting Intake Form
fields.howto_description: These seven steps turn your service list and fee sheet into an accounting client intake form that quotes each new client.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List each service and its fee
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Turn the fee sheet into rules
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each service a new client can buy, such as monthly bookkeeping or a personal return. Beside each, note the base fee and what raises it. Partnerships cost more per partner, and books that are months behind need catch-up work priced on its own.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open every intake with the client's legal name and contact details. A business also gives its EIN, the federal tax ID the IRS assigns. After that comes one section per service, shown only to clients who chose that service.
fields.howto_step_3_des: For every answer, name the document it calls for. Shares sold means a 1099-B from the broker. A stake in a partnership means a Schedule K-1 from it. Clients then upload against a list built from their own answers.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write each price as a rule the form can apply: a base amount, plus what each K-1 or added state costs. Decide which quotes a partner reviews first, and set a fallback for any work your rules do not cover.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your services and fee rules into one plain-English prompt. Emergent builds the form with its pricing logic, plus the client database behind it. When a fee changes in January, prompt the new amount and the live form updates.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Place your engagement letter after the final question with the quote filled in, and add a signature field below it. The letter should spell out the scope of services and the fee. Have your counsel review the wording once.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it as two different clients
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form as a single filer, then as a partnership in two states. Check that each sees only its own sections and that every quote matches your fee sheet. Send the live link the day a client agrees to work with you.

faq_plan.q: What is an accounting client intake form?
faq_plan.a: An accounting client intake form is the questionnaire a new client fills in before an accountant starts work. It records who the client is, which services they need, and the facts and documents each service depends on. Those answers decide what you ask for next and what the work will cost.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an accounting client intake form?
faq_plan.a: Write down the services you sell and what each one needs from a client, then describe that list in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form, its pricing logic, and the client database behind it. Fill it in yourself as a test client, and prompt each change until every service shows only its own questions.

faq_plan.q: What should a tax client intake form ask about the client's year?
faq_plan.a: Ask about what happened in the client's year in plain words, and map each event to a document behind the scenes. A new job, a home sale, a new child, or a side business each points to paperwork the client may not know by name. Ask for last year's return as well and compare the two years side by side.

faq_plan.q: What does a bookkeeping client intake form need to ask about the books?
faq_plan.a: It needs every bank, card, and loan account, the accounting software in use, and the last month each account was reconciled. Ask for monthly transaction volume too if your fee depends on it. Showing sections only to the clients who need them works the same way on a life coaching intake form or any other service intake.

faq_plan.q: How does an accounting client intake form template differ from a built form?
faq_plan.a: A template hands you a fixed list of questions. A form you build can show sections by service and price the work from the answers. Once your services and fees vary, a template's questions stop matching your work. Emergent builds that form from a plain-English prompt and changes it when you prompt again.

faq_plan.q: What questions belong in an accounting firm client intake form for business clients?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the legal name, entity type, EIN, fiscal year end, each owner and their percentage, the states the business operates in, and the software it uses for books and payroll. Entity type and owner count shape the work. A partnership, for one, uses Schedule K-1 to report each partner's share of its income. Each partner's K-1 is one more form to prepare.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect documents through a tax preparation intake form?
faq_plan.a: Give each document its own upload field, tied to the answer that calls for it, and show the client a checklist of what has arrived. Accept PDF and image files so a client can photograph a form on a phone. Label every upload with the document name and tax year. The same upload-per-answer pattern carries over to a fitness assessment form that asks for a doctor's note.

faq_plan.q: Can a tax intake form remind a client who stops halfway?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app can send email reminders on a schedule you set, such as two days after a client opens the form without submitting it, and a second one a week later. Each reminder can link straight back to the form. Stop the reminders once the client submits, and send a Slack alert to the account owner if a client still has not finished after the last one.

faq_plan.q: Can answers from an accounting client intake form sync into my accounting software?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the software has an API. Apps built with Emergent connect to any tool with an API and sync data in and out. A submitted intake can then create the client record in your ledger or practice software. Map each form field to its matching field there, then test the sync with one sample client before you send the live link.

faq_plan.q: Where does an accounting client intake form end and onboarding begin?
faq_plan.a: Intake ends with the signed engagement letter, which settles the services, the scope, and the fee. Onboarding starts after that, with access to bank feeds, payroll logins, and prior-year files. Keep intake short enough to finish in one sitting, and save the deeper setup questions for a client onboarding questionnaire.
